option.counterfactual: A theorem about the minimum number of critical points of smooth functions on S² × S² does not determine the minimum number of fixed points of time-dependent Hamiltonian maps.
option.approach: Identify exactly which version of the Arnold conjecture compares Hamiltonian fixed points with critical points, and whether that version has been proved for this manifold with degeneracy allowed. This would establish whether critical-point topology can legitimately supply the lower bound.

judge.reason: It claims that the minimum is 3, which is the same claim as e1.

options.counterfactual: Two distinct fixed points are achievable, and the usual cup-length lower bound of three does not apply to this monotone symplectic manifold.
options.approach: Audit the proposed two-fixed-point construction at the poles and along the boundaries of its local coordinate charts. The longitude argument must exclude additional fixed points everywhere, including where longitude is undefined.

options.approach: Determine the exact hypotheses of the degenerate cup-length theorem, particularly its minimal Chern number requirement. Here the minimal Chern number equals half the dimension, so a strict inequality would change the available lower bound.

options.approach: Check whether compressing a flat fixed arc through a generating function preserves smoothness, the graph condition, and Hamiltonian realizability. A failure of any one of these properties would invalidate the proposed upper bound of two.

options.counterfactual: Four fixed points are necessary even with arbitrary degeneracy, and both proposed constructions with fewer fixed points contain essential geometric errors.
options.approach: Seek a precise four-fixed-point theorem for the equal-area product of spheres, explicitly checking that it counts distinct degenerate fixed points rather than nondegenerate points or Floer generators.

options.approach: Examine whether the asserted normal form along the saddle-joining arc has an incompatible endpoint framing. Such an obstruction could prevent the ball replacement used to construct a three-critical-point function.

options.approach: Investigate whether local Floer homology and its global pairing obstruct distributing the total Floer homology among only three isolated fixed points. A rank count alone would not suffice because a degenerate point can contribute several generators.

options.counterfactual: Three is the minimum, but the autonomous saddle-merging construction is invalid; attaining three requires a genuinely time-dependent Hamiltonian.
options.approach: Audit the proposed ball replacement by comparing its boundary level sets and collar data with those of the original function. This would distinguish an actual smooth replacement from one that matches only boundary values.
